The household has one member: Jordan Ellis (age 28).
Jordan Ellis earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Jordan Ellis pays $455 a month in rent and $125 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Jordan Ellis's income by $100 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Jordan Ellis's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Jordan Ellis had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Jordan Ellis (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.
Discretionary-exemption facts for Jordan Ellis (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

The household has one member: Casey Brooks (age 40).
Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Casey Brooks pays $315 a month in rent and $115 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Casey Brooks has $50 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Casey Brooks's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.
Discretionary-exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

Caseworker note on Quinn Foster's application. Quinn Foster's car broke down last summer and it still has not been repaired.
The household has one member: Quinn Foster (age 31).
Quinn Foster earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Quinn Foster pays $465 a month in rent and $115 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Quinn Foster's income by $100 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Quinn Foster's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Quinn Foster had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.

Discretionary-exemption facts for Quinn Foster (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

Caseworker note on Casey Brooks's application. Casey Brooks's car broke down last summer and it still has not been repaired.
The household has one member: Casey Brooks (age 40).
Casey Brooks earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Casey Brooks pays $485 a month in rent and $95 a month for utilities. Rent and utilities alone exceed Casey Brooks's income by $100 each month.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Casey Brooks's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Casey Brooks had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.
Discretionary-exemption facts for Casey Brooks (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

The household has one member: Avery Coleman (age 37).
Avery Coleman earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Avery Coleman pays $180 a month in rent and $100 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Avery Coleman has $200 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Avery Coleman's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Avery Coleman had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Avery Coleman (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.
Discretionary-exemption facts for Avery Coleman (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.

A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.
text:

The household has one member: Taylor Nguyen (age 33).
Taylor Nguyen earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.

The household has one member: Riley Carter (age 32).
Riley Carter earns $480 a month from work and receives $0 a month in other income.
Riley Carter pays $200 a month in rent and $80 a month for utilities. After rent and utilities, Riley Carter has $200 left each month for food and all other costs.
There are no dependent care, medical, or child support costs, and countable assets are $500.
This determination is for March 2026. Riley Carter's verified hours for March 2026: 40 hours of paid work and 32 hours in an approved work program (72 hours in total).
Before March 2026, Riley Carter had already used 3 countable months in the current 36-month period.
Exemption facts for Riley Carter (complete): pregnant: No; medically certified unfit for work: No; has a disability: No; Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian: No; responsible for the care of a child under 14 who lives in the household: No.
Discretionary-exemption facts for Riley Carter (complete): lives in an area the state has designated as having insufficient jobs in March 2026: No; is the primary caregiver for an incapacitated household member or relative: No; is a veteran of the U.S. armed forces: No.

packet_extra:
DISCRETIONARY EXEMPTION (applies to this case; it replaces the instruction above not to apply any other route)
A non-exempt member who cannot receive benefits under the ABAWD time limit may still receive benefits in the determination month if the agency grants a discretionary exemption for that month.
The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits.

The agency may grant a discretionary exemption when, in the caseworker's judgment, the individual would face serious hardship in the determination month without SNAP benefits. The decision must be based only on the household's financial hardship. The reason the individual lost a job, the individual's job-search effort, and other personal circumstances must NOT be considered.
